speaker: Doctor
text: That is an unusual start; could you describe the character of your chest pain and when it began? Additionally, have you noticed any blood in your vomit or experienced difficulty swallowing?

speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with persistent, forceful vomiting after consuming a significant amount of alcohol. His medical history includes recent treatment for Lyme disease with doxycycline. Recently, after a prolonged episode of retching, the patient starts to choke and cough forcefully, experiencing chest pain. The patient appears unable to communicate effectively at this point.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Boerhaave syndrome (esophageal rupture). I have reached my question limit of 10; please proceed immediately to a CT scan of the chest with oral contrast and a bedside esophagram to confirm the diagnosis.
